newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Tuesday due to the approach of a new share issue on Thursday, with institutions borrowing money to prepare for the issue, traders said.
Turnover surged to 13.1 million lots from 8.99 million on Monday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract edged up to 13.62 percent from 13.17 percent.
"The new issue attracted interest on the repo market today, in particular from institutions," a trader said. He said the rates were likely to remain at high levels in the coming days.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to heavy selling by some big institutions on rumours that the exchange would abolish the same-day settlement system, traders said. Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.81 million lots from 1.93 million.
The most active three-year bond that matures in August 1999 ended at 103.75 yuan, down from 104.30 yuan.
"The market was dominated by institutional selling today," one trader said. "They sold on a large scale on rumours after having won heavy profits thanks to surges in late August."
